amended_control.C6a_kappa_identical: UNCHANGED from C6: 10 targets x 2 reviewers with identical verdicts -> kappa = 1.0 within 1e-9.
amended_control.C6b_kappa_independent_200x2: 10x2 -> 200x2 targets, seed 20260912; |kappa| < 0.20. The larger design concentrates the estimator (SE ~0.05) so this is a valid implementation test.
amended_control.C6c_kappa_null_calibration: Monte Carlo null for the ORIGINAL 10x2 design: 2000 seeded random designs, report mean/sd/2.5th/97.5th percentiles; require the observed 10x2 kappa (-0.44) to lie inside the central 95% interval. This documents that the original design's noise, not over-dispersion of the implementation, produced the failure.

diagnosis.C5: Instrument defect, not a measurement disagreement. Two Counter.most_common() outputs (M1 unknown_token_top, M3 top_reviewers) break count ties by insertion order, so reversing the corpus changed the rendered examples while all metric values were identical. Fix: deterministic tie-break by (count desc, label asc). No metric definition changes.
diagnosis.C6: Mis-calibrated control, not an implementation defect. The pre-registered criterion was '10 targets x 2 reviewers with seeded independent verdicts -> |kappa| < 0.20'. At the frozen seed 20260912 the randomized 10x2 design yields Fleiss kappa = -0.44000000000000006. With 10 subjects and 4 categories the standard error of kappa is of order 0.2-0.3, so the pre-registered acceptance bound is not a valid test of the estimator: a correct estimator fails it about half the time. C6a (identical verdicts -> kappa = 1.0) passed in the same run.

measurement_disclosure: The bring-up run was measurement-complete before the control review (it wrote a report with controls.status=FAIL and exit 3). Its M1/M2/M3 values are preserved in the archived failing report and are reproduced by the post-amendment run; the amendment changes no metric definition, so no value is re-interpreted. Only instrument-internal control evaluation changed.
